title: Negative control is hand-written pre-fix code, not derived from the shipped scrub minus the guard — it can drift from the true pre-fix shape on a refactor
detail: Unlike the positive tests, the negative control is not extracted from form_view.gleam — it is a hard-coded duplicate of the pre-fix scrub. If the shipped snippet is refactored, this copy can silently diverge from the true pre-fix logic while staying green. Verified: the suite still bites independently, because removing the guard from the shipped function turns the positive test red (empirically reproduced: unguarded scrub throws NoModificationAllowedError and fires the setter), so this is a durability nit, not a coverage hole.
recommended_fix: Derive the negative control from the extracted shipped source by deleting the two guard statements (or the guard branch) at test time, then assert the result throws on the fake element — keeps it anchored to shipped bytes.
